item.title: Lorri Cramer is known as the Turtle Lady of Manhattan and one summer she took in 680 babies
item.description: In the heart of Manhattan, Lorri Cramer, famously known as the Turtle Lady, dedicates her life to rescuing and rehabilitating injured and abandoned turtles. Her mission, not only to restore their health but also to secure safe environments for their future, has brought to light the troubling issue of non-native turtles being wrongfully released into inappropriate habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Ohio landlord mistakenly throws away tenant's loved belongings; court upholds $6,000 award
item.description: Grace Davis was awarded $6,000 by an Ohio court after her landlord mistakenly discarded her personal belongings. Despite lacking receipts or photographs, she provided a detailed list with estimated values. The landlord's management company challenged the award, arguing that sufficient proof was missing. The appeals court upheld the ruling, stating that the unique nature of the items justified Davis's valuation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: More than 8,000 people applied to be NASA astronauts last time and just 10 were picked
item.description: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: An LA diner that served generations since 1924 shut down in 2025, has reopened under a nonprofit operator
item.description: After a lengthy shutdown in 2025 due to property issues, Original Pantry Cafe in Los Angeles has triumphantly reopened! With new management from Hope the Mission, the cafe will utilize its profits to bolster homelessness services. Diners can still indulge in the beloved classic menu while also enjoying fresh additions. Although hours have shifted, there are plans to bring back 24-hour service.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: As ice receded on a Swiss Alpine pass, archaeologists discovered a 4,000 years old bronze neck ring
item.description: A remarkable discovery at Lötschen Pass has unearthed a 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring, making it the first metal artifact found at this significant historical site. While previous discoveries were primarily organic materials preserved in ice, this find suggests that ancient peoples may have practiced mobility through Alpine passes, connecting various regions. Experts speculate that the ring could have served as a ritual offering or token of gratitude.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Indiana man paid $9,489 towards condo debt after $9,213 judgment, but court says he still owes more
item.description: Onnie James Florence Jr. encountered significant legal troubles stemming from his failure to pay homeowners' association fees for his condominium in Indiana. After acquiring the unit, he neglected to keep up with payments while residing in Illinois. The Meridian Arch Owners Association successfully secured a default judgment against him for the overdue fees. Despite making a partial payment later, additional fees remained unpaid, prompting ongoing legal action.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dua Lipa's £6.75 million London home renovation set to finish in 2027
item.description: Dua Lipa is making waves with the transformation of her Victorian home in Hampstead, which includes an ambitious plan for a luxurious basement pool. After encountering numerous setbacks, the project received the green light to commence construction in 2024. Local environmental concerns have prompted strict adherence to regulations, pushing the anticipated completion to 2027. With an investment estimated at around £3 million, this renovation underscores its intricate and grand vision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists flew drones through humpback whales' breath off Canada and sequenced entire genomes
item.description: Researchers at the University of St Andrews have pioneered a groundbreaking technique to harness whale DNA through the use of drones. This method captures genetic material from the whales' breath, often referred to as whale snot. Their findings successfully sequenced complete genomes from specimens gathered off the coast of British Columbia.

item.title: Texas Fraud Charges: Man allegedly won 70 contracts; counterfeit gear raises concerns
item.description: Marcelo Fascino, a 24-year-old from San Antonio, Texas, stands accused of securing more than $1.6 million in federal contracts by deceitfully claiming his business was owned by veterans. He allegedly misrepresented his military background, impersonated government officials, and manipulated suppliers to stifle competition. Furthermore, investigators found he sold counterfeit military gear, mislabeling it as American-made but failing to meet specifications. He faces several charges as the investigation proceeds.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Beverly Hills penthouse sells for $21M, with rooftop pool and $18,740 monthly dues
item.description: In a stunning real estate move, a penthouse in Beverly Hills has shattered local records by selling for $21 million within just 10 days of listing. Initially priced at $27.5 million, the luxe property ultimately changed hands for 24% less, showcasing its many high-end amenities and hotel-style services for residents. The fortunate buyer also saved over $1 million in transfer taxes by opting for Beverly Hills over Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New York couple give 77 acres to protect drinking water and preserve wildlife
item.description: Jerry and Joanne Braun donated approximately 77 acres of land to the Town of Newburgh. This land donation aims to protect the drinking water supply sourced from the Chadwick Lake Reservoir. The couple requested reimbursement for subdividing the land, not seeking payment for it. Residents will still have access for passive recreational activities like hiking and enjoying nature.

item.title: Brooklyn man removed from US in 1999 wins right to seek sale of home he bought with his wife
item.description: Clyde and Verna Nelson's shared Brooklyn home has been at the center of a complicated legal battle following their divorce. Recently, the New York appeals court concluded that Clyde retains the right to initiate the sale of their co-owned property, dismissing Verna's claims that his rights were nullified by their divorce.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michael Sheen-backed children's hospice appeal raises £264,695 in 56 hours
item.description: Tŷ Hafan, a remarkable children's hospice located in Wales, has triumphed by surpassing its fundraising goal during the Every Precious Life campaign. Over just two days, generous public donations and match funding totaled an impressive £264,695. The heartfelt appeal, inspired by the touching story of William Watkins, attracted support from various Welsh celebrities. These funds will significantly enhance the hospice's ability to support families facing life-limiting conditions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Glenvar Heights Record Sale: Mansion sells for $13.25 million; nearly doubles in value
item.description: In a noteworthy real estate transaction, a luxurious mansion in Glenvar Heights has been sold for an impressive $13.25 million, nearly doubling its original price. Jose Dans Jr. had acquired the property for $7.3 million just in 2024, transforming it into a lavish estate complete with a main house, guesthouse, and cabana.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million to anyone who can solve one big problem standing in the way of building a human settlement on the Moon
item.description: NASA has launched the Moon Base Challenge, encouraging students to develop solutions for lunar habitation. The initiative offers $1 million in prizes to student teams from high schools and universities. Teams will focus on areas like power generation, life-support systems, and astronaut safety to address the complexities of lunar living. Registration for the competition is open until January 25, 2027, to eligible educational institutions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
